newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst plans new biotech research.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst plans new biotech research.

text.p: German chemical giant Hoechst AG said Wednesday it planned to set up a small biotechnology research facility near Munich that would also do genetic work.

A Hoechst spokesman, responding to a telephone inquiry, said around 20 researchers would be employed in rented premises there but denied a magazine report that the company had plans to build a full biotechnology centre.

German magazine Wirtschaftswoche said in a pre-release of an article slated to appear Thursday that Hoechst would be restarting genetics research in the new premises after four years absence from Germany.

It said Hoechst had moved its genetics research activities to the United States following resistance it encountered from local government officials in Hesse, the region in which its Frankfurt head offices are based.
The magazine quoted a Hoechst executive as saying that cooperation with German officials had since improved.

The Hoechst spokesman refused to confirm the quotes but, when asked if the planned activities would include genetics research, he replied the Munich team would be looking at all aspects of biotechnology.
